guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our model is a little less aggressive on Ohio State than the market, but we understand why the price is so large. We see a top-tier Ohio State passing offense facing an Illinois pass defense that has struggled by pass EPA, while Illinois' rushing offense runs into one of the strongest rush defenses in our numbers. We also project a major Ohio State advantage in preventing scoring opportunities, which makes it difficult to build a strong underdog case around sustained Illinois drives.

Where we retain some restraint is Ohio State's defensive turnover. We see only three returning defensive starters from 2025 after eight departed, so we are not simply carrying last season's dominant results forward without adjustment. At the same time, Ohio State returns eight offensive starters and entered 2026 with substantial offensive-line continuity. For us, the modest disagreement with the market is not enough because the matchup advantages still point heavily toward Ohio State, particularly when Illinois has the ball.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are focused on Ohio State's passing offense against the Illinois pass defense. Julian Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns in 2025, and Jeremiah Smith opened 2026 with eight catches for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half against Ball State. We do not treat one opener as proof of what happens here, but that established efficiency and receiving talent directly attack the weakest part of Illinois' statistical profile. If Illinois cannot limit explosive and efficient passing production, our slightly more conservative view of the margin will face immediate pressure.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards, including 434 passing and 237 rushing, while allowing 165 total yards.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half against Ball State.
Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry against Ball State and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Fourteen Ohio State players recorded a reception against Ball State, the program's first game with at least 14 receivers catching a pass since Sept. 22, 2018.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in the opener against Ball State.
Freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards against Ball State and scored on his first career reception.

opponent_notes.fact: Ohio State's schedule lists a home game against Illinois on Sept. 26, 2026.
Cornerback Devin Sanchez recorded a 2025 season-high five tackles and a pass breakup against Illinois.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is a returning offensive starter and entered 2026 with 15 starts in 19 career games.

Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025, led the nation in completion percentage, ranked second nationally with a 177.5 efficiency rating, and threw for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Sayin's 77.0 completion percentage in 2025 set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Sayin has seven career 300-yard passing games.
Sayin was selected as one of Ohio State's seven captains for 2026.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns eight offensive starters: QB Julian Sayin, RB Bo Jackson, WR Jeremiah Smith, WR Brandon Inniss, OT Phillip Daniels, C Carson Hinzman, OG Luke Montgomery and OG Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Bo Jackson rushed for a team-high 1,090 yards on 179 carries in 2025 and had six 100-yard games in his first 12 outings.
Jeremiah Smith entered 2026 with 171 receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns across his college career.
Transfer wide receiver Devin McCuin arrived from UTSA after recording 65 receptions for 726 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025; he has 28 career starts.
Transfer wide receiver Kyle Parker arrived from LSU with seven career starts and career totals of 34 receptions, 385 yards and five touchdowns.
Tight end Hunter Welcing transferred from Northwestern with 11 career starts, while tight end Mason Williams transferred from Ohio with 26 career starts.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns three defensive starters from 2025: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.
Defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025 and entered 2026 with 9.5 career sacks.
Safety Jaylen McClain made 53 tackles and played 816 defensive snaps in 2025.

Ohio State added defensive transfers James Smith and Qua Russaw from Alabama, Christian Alliegro from Wisconsin, John Walker from UCF, Beau Atkinson from North Carolina, Earl Little Jr. from Florida State and Terry Moore from Duke.
Wisconsin transfer linebacker Christian Alliegro entered 2026 with 127 career tackles, eight sacks and 12 career starts.
Florida State transfer safety Earl Little Jr. led Florida State with 76 tackles in 2025 and entered 2026 with 97 career tackles and four interceptions.
UCF transfer defensive tackle John Walker entered 2026 with 64 career tackles, eight tackles for loss and 13 career starts.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are Matt Patricia on defense, Arthur Smith on offense and Robby Discher on special teams.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Tim Walton is co-defensive coordinator and secondary coach, Matt Guerrieri is pass game coordinator and safeties coach, and James Laurinaitis coaches the linebackers.

offensive_context.fact: Ohio State entered 2026 with 85.8 percent of its 2025 offensive-line snaps returning among linemen who played at least 100 snaps, the highest listed rate among Power Four teams.
After the Ball State opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
Center Carson Hinzman entered 2026 with 36 starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Ohio State was one of two FBS programs to produce a 3,500-yard passer, a 1,000-yard receiver and a 1,000-yard rusher in each of the previous two seasons.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed 9.3 points and 219.1 total yards per game in 2025, ranking first nationally in scoring defense and total defense.
Ohio State allowed 129.7 passing yards per game in 2025 and 8.73 yards per completion.
Ohio State allowed 12 touchdowns from scrimmage during the 2025 season.
In the 2026 opener, Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing yards and 120 passing yards, and allowed conversions on 21.4 percent of third downs.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's only returning specialist starter.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann from the 2025 team.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State entered the season with 34 returning letterwinners and 31 letterwinners lost.
Ohio State was listed as the 11th-youngest team nationally, fifth-youngest in the Power Four and second-youngest in the Big Ten, with an average age of 19.95.
